review_summary: F1850 completes the donor-recovery task. All four cases now have meshes generated from recovered donors (Cases 1 and 3 were blocked in F1849), and verifiable donor provenance is established in the repo via compact JSON snapshots — an accepted alternative to the binary ODBs the F1850 instruction requested, which the repository forbids and GitHub's 100 MB limit prevents. Cases 2 and 5 reproduce the F1849 controls EXACTLY, confirmed not only by count but by identical mesh body SHA (Case 2: 6BCD710B..., Case 5: 438C9FEA...), which independently corroborates the snapshot-to-minimal-ODB roundtrip. Case 1 is 20,193 versus F1779's 20,232 (-0.19%, no exact reproduction claimed). Case 3 is 45,009 versus F1779's 9,975 (+351%) — honestly reported and explained: F1779's Case 3 used selected stress-recovery states, not the damage envelope, so all-damage sizing does not reproduce F1779's Case 3. The report states plainly that a uniform damage strategy is not qualified as reproducing F1779 across four benchmarks. The framework is unchanged, frozen assets are preserved, 0 new PBS, cumulative 36. CORRECTION OWED BY THE REVIEWER: my F1849 review stated the Case 5 donor was 'purely elastic' with 'no evolving damage'. That was not established. The executor reports donor inspection found maxSDV1 about 0.476, so the donor does contain damage; the coarse 4,375-element mesh is therefore not explained by an absence of damage. That F1849 characterization is withdrawn. The maxSDV1 value itself is executor-reported (the snapshot contains the constructed MISESERI, not SDV1, so it is not independently verifiable from the repo).

gaps.title: Case 3 all-damage mesh does not reproduce F1779 (45,009 versus 9,975, +351%)
gaps.detail: The all-damage Case 3 mesh is 45,009 elements, 4.5x F1779's 9,975, and the image shows dense refinement across most of the 65x120 mm plate rather than F1779's extremely narrow dual bands. This is honestly reported and explained (F1779's Case 3 used selected stress-recovery states, not the damage envelope), and the report states plainly that a uniform damage strategy is not qualified as reproducing F1779 across four benchmarks. It is a scientific finding about the damage-envelope method, not a defect in the donor-recovery execution, and it does not block approval of this correction-only task.

findings.finding: Genuine mesh, visually inspected. Title states 20,193 elements, 97.30% quads, Gate 06 1.919x FAIL, CONSTRUCTED_DAMAGE_ENVELOPE. A dense band follows the crack ligament (y approx 0.5) from the notch tip (x approx 0.5) to the right edge, densest near the tip; the rest of the plate is coarser. The pattern is consistent with the F1779 narrow-band description and the count is within 0.19% of F1779's 20,232. The FAIL is stated honestly in the title.

Genuine mesh, visually inspected. Title states 17,280 elements, 97.25% quads, Gate 06 2.205x PASS, CONSTRUCTED_DAMAGE_ENVELOPE. A narrow dense band lies distal to the hole (x approx 0.75-1.0, y approx 0.6-0.7) with a dense patch at the notch-to-hole ligament; the rest is coarse. The pattern matches the F1849 Case 2 image and the F1779 narrow-band description. The mesh body SHA is identical to the F1849 Case 2 mesh, confirming exact reproduction.

Genuine mesh, visually inspected. Title states 45,009 elements, 97.29% quads, Gate 06 2.004x PASS, CONSTRUCTED_DAMAGE_ENVELOPE. The 65x120 mm plate is densely refined across most of its area, with very dense regions around all three holes, the notch, and the primary/secondary corridors. This is NOT the narrow dual-band pattern of F1779's 9,975-element mesh; it is a broad, diffuse refinement. The image visually confirms the +351% count and the finding that all-damage sizing does not reproduce F1779's Case 3. The PASS (2.004x, just above 2.0x) is stated in the title.

Genuine mesh, visually inspected. Title states 4,375 elements, 96.59% quads, Gate 06 1.338x FAIL, CONSTRUCTED_DAMAGE_ENVELOPE. The mesh is coarse overall: seven holes visible with only modest refinement around hole perimeters and inter-hole ligaments, no dense inter-hole band. The image matches the F1849 Case 5 image, and the mesh body SHA is identical to the F1849 Case 5 mesh, confirming exact reproduction. The FAIL is stated honestly in the title.
